Concluding the 2-part story arc "Headhunting!" Black Alice is torn between good and evil. For which side should she use her magical abilities? As the Huntress and Black Canary pull her towards the Birds, powerful others are influencing Alice's darker tendencies.

There's an eerily familiar Caped Crusader running around the Birds' territory...one that's freaking out Huntress and Black Canary. But Oracle's life will be the most affected by this heroine's bizarre return!

Notes:

  • The cover is a homage of the cover of Detective Comics #359.

It's time for a change in the Birds' outfit, and the writing is on the computer screen that at least one member of the team will be moving on. With issue #100 just around the corner, now seems the perfect time for a reality check.

Amanda Waller organizes the Suicide Squad for a mission to take down a Qurac terrorist group known as the Jihad before they can attack the U.S.

Things starts off with the Jihad, a Qurac terrorist group of super-villains involved a live training exercise. They utilize their powers effectively and in a devastatingly coordinated effort. At the end of the demonstration, a deal is made to buy their services. The target: within the United States.

Mr. Economos gives Vicki Vale a tour of the Belle Reve facility. The apparent harshness of the conditions is demonstrated by the treatment of the Parasite. The Parasite is being kept unconscious and fed just enough to keep him alive. A rat is mechanically shoved through a cage every few hours for his parasitic energy to leach the life force from. Although it seems inhumane, it is a somewhat necessary process as the Parasite is an extremely dangerous individual who could kill any guards that come too close.

Amanda Waller confers with the staff psychologists, Dr. LaGrieve and Ms. Herrs. They discuss the different Suicide Squad team members and their psychological profiles. It is rather questionable whether most of the members are really fit for duty, but Amanda asserts her authority and makes the decision to proceed anyways.

The debriefing. Amanda goes over the members of the Jihad and the plans for Task Force X (aka the Suicide Squad) to infiltrate "Jotunheim", base of the Jihad.

On boarding the plane to take them to their mission, Rick Flagg encounters an old love, Karin.

It's Batman versus Amanda Waller as the Dark Knight discovers the existence of the Suicide Squad and doesn't take too well to the idea!

Batman infiltrated Belle Reve to confirm if the Suicide Squad is real. After confronting Amanda Waller, telling her that he will blow the whistle on the covert government team, Batman seems like he has the upper hand. However, Amanda Waller informs Batman that she will use all of her extensive resources to find out who Batman really is and report that to the media as well. Feeling stymied, Batman reluctantly agrees to keep the Suicide Squad a secret until he can find another way to take them down.

Meet the Squad's newest leader! Speedy leads the Squad on a mission with Boomerang, Nightshade, Enchantress and Black Orchid against a Colombian drug king!

Mari McCabe, better known to the world as Vixen, returns to her job as a professional model. She's working on a tropical shoot when she gets a few moments to go swimming. When she returns, everyone on the crew, including the other models, are killed by gunshots because some of the pictures captured an illegal drug deal. This action gets the attention of the Suicide Squad who has to go undercover to infiltrate the drug dealers stronghold.

The mission in Colombia continues, and in true Squad style, everything goes wrong! Vixen and Black Orchid are trapped and the only one who can rescue them seems to be the mentally unstable Enchantress!

The Suicide Squad destroy the cocaine supply of the drug dealer who killed associates of the Vixen. Vixen herself kills the drug dealer, named Cujo, and wonders if she's lost her soul to the animal totem that gives her power.

The Justice League International and the Suicide Squad have a stand off inside a Russian prison--with the life of Nemesis at stake!

This is a continuation of JLI #13

The Suicide Squad enters Russia to free their teammate, Nemesis. Unfortunately, the Justice League International arrives as well to stop them from committing an international incident. The two teams clash, particularly Rick Flag and Batman, but some of the members find a common group and call a truce. The Justice League International decides to hold Nemesis in their embassy while the Suicide Squad makes an escape.

The Squad's latest mission: rescue Nightshade's brother from the Land of the Nightshade, a place where he's been trapped for a decade.

An irate Amanda Waller arrives at the Oval Office for a scheduled meeting with the president.He then introduces her to Senator Cray,while charging her and the Suicide Squad to ensure his reelection much to her disgust. Tolliver then arrives informing them if they don't cooperate they will reveal all the details of Task Force X and if she is unable to do it Tolliver will take over her position.Meanwhile in Russia the KGB infiltrate the embassy looking for Nemesis, only to learn he's no longer there.

While at Belle Reeve Waller arrives not even mentioning their botched rescue mission of Nemesis before telling Eve her private mission will be carried out tomorrow and to assemble a team.Meanwhile Deadshot meets with his therapist Marnie Herrs,but storms out feeling the therapy won't work.Meanwhile Bronze Tiger takes Captain Boomerang out for drinks,before he passes out and is taken back to Belle Reeve to participate in the mission when he awakens.Nightshade then takes the squad to the Land of the Nightshades,where they are attacked by the Incubus in control of Nightshade's brother Larry.

There's more trouble brewing in Washington...and that's the best news the Squad's heard all day. It's the fate of the Enchantress and the change in Nightshade's brother that's really got them down.

The Incubus in control of Larry manages to capture each member of the Squad,who then tells Nightshade the story of how he came to be possessed by the Incubus who reveals his intention of mating with Nightshade.However June soon transforms into the Enchantress.Enchantress then begins her battle with the Incubus infused Larry,refusing to release the team as she intends to murder them afterwards.He then reveals the entity empowering the enchantress is in actuality the Sucubus before removing it and preparing to implant it in Eve so they may mate and produce a vessel for Azhmodeus.However Duchess breaks free and manages to free the others with several shops as they attempt to keep the Incubus away from Nightshade,while the Incubus turns Vixen on the Bronze Tiger due to the animilistic nature of the dimension.

Bronze Tiger manages to incapacitate Vixen as Larry makes Nightshade his equal, as she attacks him.The battle begins to destroy the reality there in, as Deadshot shoots Larry in the head as they all link hands and fall.

In the final part of the odyssey, the Squad takes a wrong turn...and winds up in the Meta Zone, home dimension to one of DC's strangest heroes: Shade the Changing Man!

As the Squad continues spinning from the destruction of the reality they had been in, Eve opens a portal which takes the Squad to another strange realm before Eve passes out. The Squad is then attacked by natives of the new dimension, as Bronze Tiger leads them into battle while a stranger wonders from a far where the Squad has come from.The Stranger then attacks driving off the monsters, before using Nightshade and his vest to teleport him and the Squad out of the realm.They then teleport back to Belle Reeve as Waller has Shade report to the briefing room to fill them in on his urgent mission.He then fills the Squad with the addition of Captain Cold in on the three dimensions.

The Squad with the returning Rick Flag then leave to stop Wizor.They defeat his students as Shade leaves with the Suicide Squad.

Just when it looks like the Squad can take some time off, the Jihad holds Manhattan for ransom, demanding a rematch to the death.

The Jihad enter Manhattan, causing terrorists attacks, to get the attention of the Suicide Squad.

The Jihad brings its worst to Manhattan...but the Suicide Squad is right on its tail. Plus, the debut of the all-new Nightshade!

The Jihad are defeated by the members of the Suicide Squad.

In a stand-alone tale, operating the Squad hasn't been without cost, as Amanda Waller discovers when she pauses to reflect on the lost souls that form the team.

It's a day in the life of Amanda Waller as she works in Belle Reve, the boss of the Suicide Squad.

The Squad takes the fight to Qurac to put an end to the Jihad before the terrorist organization can go on its first mission--and one of the Squad isn't coming back alive!

The Suicide Squad enters Quarac to defeat the Jihad, which they do successfully. True to their name, though, not all the members of the Suicide Squad survive the experience.

The Flash villain Mirror Master is on the loose committing crimes throughout the city, but when he's caught by the Squad, they learn that there just might be a trick to this mirror.

Captain Boomerang, masquerading as the Mirror Master to commit crimes anonymously, gets caught with his deception by Amanda Waller and the Suicide Squad.
The election race is on and Senator Cray demands action from the Squad. What will happen? To start with, Flag goes AWOL and Amanda has a showdown with Derek Tolliver.
Amanda Waller's problems with Senator Joe Cray finally come to a head and Deadshot pays the ultimate sacrifice.

Featuring the first appearance of Barbara Gordon as Oracle! The Squad splits up to fight the invading aliens in Russia and Australia!

The Suicide Squad battles against the Invasion. This is the first appearance of Oracle
While Amanda Waller must face the Senate, the Suicide Squad finds themselves in Africa for a mission.
Amanda Waller deals with the public outing of the Suicide Squad and takes some measures to remain in charge.

Rick Flag decides to go to the base of the Jihad to destroy them where it hurts--and heads to plant a bomb in their base!

Rick Flag decides to go to the base of the Jihad to destroy them where it hurts. After implanting a bomb, he is attacked by the leader of the Jihad, Rustam. It seems they have died in the explosion.

Part 2: The Force of July is the first American espionage group to fall as an evil mastermind (or two) foments inter-agency war.

Notes:

  • Part 1 started in Checkmate #15.
  • Part 3 continues in Checkmate #16.

  • The cover is a homage to the cover of Fantastic Four #249.

Part 4 of the Janus Directive story arc. As the government agencies continue to wage war against each other, Kobra, prepares to strike. Vixen, Duchess, Count Vertigo, and Shade are sent by Amanda Waller to capture Dr. Megala. During their attempt to do so they run into Major Force and Peacemaker.

Notes:

  • Part 3 continues from Checkmate #16.
  • Part 5 continues in Checkmate #17.

issue_title: The Janus Directive part 8 - Heavy Squad
description:
"The Janus Directive" part 8. Belle Reve comes under attack as dark forces strive to destroy American intelligence agencies.

Notes:

  • Part 7 continues from Firestorm, the Nuclear Man #86.
  • Part 9 continues in Checkmate #18.

The Squad returns to Belle Reve for some rest, however, the rest won't last long because Darkseid has decided it's time for G. Gordon Godfrey to come home and dispatches the Female Furies to bring him back!

The Female Furies arrive from Apokolips to Earth to return Glorious Godfrey to his home planet and face Darkseid. Glorious Godfrey was placed in Belle Reve, a prison that also holds the secret headquarters of the Suicide Squad. A battle ensues, though the Female Furies are able to kidnap Glorious Godfrey and escape. However, upon entering their Boom-Tube to leave, Bernadeth and Lashina fight each other, leaving their fates to be undetermined.

"The Janus Directive" part 10, The various government agencies must unite together in order to stop Kobra's plans.

It's time to unite the American espionage forces to destroy the madman Kobra and his flying fortress.

Notes:

  • Part 9 continues from Checkmate #18.
  • Part 11 concludes in Captain Atom #30.
Away with her child, Amanda Waller reviews her notes on Father Richard Craemer and his effect on the Suicide Squad.
The Suicide Squad, with the help of Shade the Changing Man, must accept a mission of rescue.

Duchess is ready to return home...to Apokolips, and she's bringing a handpicked team with her.

Squad member Duchess reveals she is Lashina, a member of Darkseid's Female Furies. She decides she's going back home and the perfect present to assauge her brutal masters is most of the Squad! Bullets fly and bodies will fall ...

Lashina reveals all while the Squad takes the scenic tour of Armagetto and has the fight of their lives. Also, Amanda Waller versus Granny Goodness.

Lashina and the Suicide Squad arrive on Apokolips and engage in combat with Granny Goodness and the Female Furies. Meanwhile, back on Earth, Bronze Tiger works to assemble a rescue team.

Bronze Tiger and Deadshot lead a rescue team to Apokolips to save Amanda and the rest of the Squad...but who's going to save them?

Issue Tagline: Female Fury
The Squad closes ranks in a desperate attempt to escape from Apokolips...but not everyone will get home alive! The Forever People guest-star.

The Squad returns from Apokolips, and not without several casualties and even some deaths. The Loa continues its secret maneuverings, and the identity of the mysterious pie-thrower is finally revealed.

Learn the history of Ben Turner, as Sarge Steel tries to crack the Bronze Tiger. Plus, Jewelee learns something that changes her life.

First time Barbara Gordon is named as the Oracle.
The Suicide Squad has been shut down--but that doesn't stop Amanda Waller from leading ex-members on a raid to destroy the Loa.

William Hell incites racist riots and Amanda Waller sends in the Squad to quell the rising hate and stop the vile supremacist.

William Hell makes the scene, inciting racism. Amanda Waller and the Suicide Squad make their move to stop him.
After a year of imprisonment, Sarge Steel makes Amanda Waller an offer that'll get her out of prison: start up the Suicide Squad again.

Since their disbandment, the Squad members have gone their separate ways. Now it's up to the unlikely team of Amanda Waller and the Dark Knight to bring them back together. "The Phoenix Gambit" part 2.
In order to prevent a confrontation between American and Soviet forces in the war-torn country Vlatava, Batman and the Suicide Squad head to Europe.
The Suicide Squad must complete their mission in Europe in order to gain their freedom--and become independent agents.
One hero falls and another rises in their place. Meanwhile, Captain Boomerang attends his mother's funeral and learns a secret about his past.

The Suicide Squad meets their wits' end fighting with a new group called Hayoth. However, there's no rest for the wicked when their primary objective, Kobra, joins the party.

Notes:

  • The cover is a homage to the cover of The X-Men #100.
The Suicide Squad and Hayoth join forces to fight against Kobra, but Amanda Waller has her own set of terms for the team's cooperation.
As the battle against Kobra continues, the teams quickly realize their combined powers may not be enough--prompting Raven to take Kobra on single-handedly!
Oracle/Barbara Gordon/Batgirl (Birds of Prey) cover and story; Flashback scene where Oracle (Barbara Gordon) gets crippled by the Joker (The Killing Joke).
The New Thinker has taken control of Amanda Waller's mind and is now running the Suicide Squad, but his real target is none other than Oracle.

The Squad is sent into Russia to bring back a now-famous dissident, but getting in and around the USSR is no easy deal, especially when they will have a wanted prisoner with them, so the Squad is bringing along the Penguin for the ride.

The Suicide Squad enters Russia to liberate a political prisoner... a prisoner who does not want to be freed!
Amanda Waller puts together a special team that includes Suicide Squad founding members Nemesis, Nightshade, Bronze Tiger, and Deadshot for a personal mission to preserve the legacy of Rick Flag.

Deadshot's costume has been missing for months, and when he tracks it down, he finds it in the hands of another.

Deadshot gets his uniform and guns stolen by a naive man. Unfortunately Floyd is unprepared mentally to deal with fighting 'himself'.

issue_title: The Death and Life and Death and Life and Death and Life of Dr. Light
description: The unexpected return of an ex-Squad member in the most offbeat tale yet. Prepare for the death and life of Doctor Light!

"The Dragon's Horde" part 1! Amanda and the Squad are hired by the Japanese government to recover the Dragon's Horde, a cache of Soviet weaponry hidden in Cambodia.

A long last cache of weapons holds many dangers and the Squad is sent to deal with the problem. Unfortunately other dangers beset them, not the least of which is their new member's desire to kill them all.

The Squad moves into position throughout the Far East, bringing them up against the Red Shadows, the Yakuza, and the Khmer Rouge. "The Dragon's Horde" part 2.

The Squad strives to destroy a dangerous cache of weapons. Their newest member, however, wants to kill them all and their only defense is a nasty bluff.

The Yakuza prepares to execute Amanda Waller while Deadshot, Count Vertigo, and Steelwolf go up against the Khmer Rouge. "The Dragon's Horde" part 3.

The new Atom fights to protect Amanda Waller from assassins.
With the members of the Squad all captured or surrounded, it's up to one person to save the day: the Atom! "The Dragon's Horde" part 4.

As the Atom defends Amanda Waller from the Yakuza and their meta-human assassin, the New Thinker and Captain Boomerang struggle to escape the clutches of the Soviet Dead Men.

Russian and American super-agents clash over a secret shipment of weapons. "The Dragon's Horde" finale.

The Suicide Squad enters the War of the Gods as Chaos shakes the world.

A secondary squad is sent in to gain intelligence from the island fortress of Circe. This includes the author avatar of Grant Morrison, one of many whom do not make it back alive.
Batman, Superman, and Aquaman suspect that Amanda Waller had a hand in the death of Ray Palmer, but when they seek to question the Squad, they find resistance from the Jihad and Hayoth.

It's a wild ride across the freezing terrain of Russia as the team seeks asylum after their rescue mission goes awry and the Russian military mobilizes against them.

The Suicide Squad try to make their way to an American Embassy in Russia after liberating a political prisoner. At the embassy, the Suicide Squad realize they caused an international incident and they have to either turn themselves in or have the American government turn them in. Meanwhile, Nightshade is pushing her powers to the limit.

The Suicide Squad face the combined might of Superman, Batman, and Aquaman!

An imprisoned Middle Eastern dictator brings the interest of a super-powered terrorist group. They attack the base the man is being held captive at. The Justice League arrives to safeguard innocent lives.

Superman, Batman, and Aquaman try to unlock the mystery behind the Cabal while the new Atom is sent by Amanda Waller to infiltrate the Microforce.

An imprisoned Middle Eastern dictator causes the Squad and the JLA and other super-powered beings multiple problems.

Ray Palmer returns to avenge the death of Adam Cray!

The new Atom deals with tiny espionage agents. Who will survive? Well, look at the title.

Inhabitants of the Island of Diabloverde claim association to the Suicide Squad—a lie Amanda Waller intends to get to the bottom of no matter the cost.

Amanda Waller learns that in a small island country called Diabloverde are a group of super-villains masquerading as the Suicide Squad.

Notes:

  • The cover is a homage to the cover of Justice League #1.

issue_title: Nasty As They Want To Be
description:
The Suicide Squad is commanded to overthrow the dictator of Diabloverde while the Cabal sends Task Force X after Amanda Waller.

Deadshot deals with the emotional ramifications of his outfit being stolen.
Amanda Waller and the Suicide Squad confront Task Force X, but the jungle island of Diabloverde forces each member of the team to confront their darkest fears.

Final Issue! Amanda Waller and what remains of the Suicide Squad face a villain that may be as powerful and cold-hearted as Death itself.

The Squad's quest to stop an island dictator could end in the jungle; all who travel through it are forced to face their deepest fears.

Count Vertigo also faces deep personal emotion problems without the 'assistance' of jungle plants.

Original SUICIDE SQUAD writer John Ostrander and Gail Simone resurrect The Suicide Squad as they take on BLACKEST NIGHT and the Secret Six! The Fiddler has risen from the dead, and he's targeting Deadshot and anyone who stands in his way. But someone else has targeted Deadshot – the Suicide Squad! Everything is about to hit the Wall (Amanda Waller, that is) – and this Wall hits back! Continuing this month's one-issue revival of classic DC Universe titles, this epic story carries into January's SECRET SIX #17!

The Suicide Squad is on the run, Enchantress has lost contact with reality, and Nightshade is hurt! What could possible complicate matters? Russia sending in the People's Heroes to aid their army!

The Suicide Squad, attacked by the People's Heroes, finally leaves Russia but the political prisoner they came to liberate dies.

After the team's last mission, it's time for a breather. But as they say, no rest for the wicked, as personal trials and tribulations cause sparks of various sorts to fly.

Doctor Simon La Grieve goes over his case studies of the various members of the Suicide Squad.

1. Cover by Jerry Bingham.
  2. Written by John Ostrander, penciled by Luke McDonnell, inked by Bob Lewis, colored by Carl Gafford and lettered by Todd Klein and John Costanza.

Notes:

  • Cover connects with Detective Comics #582, Captain Atom #11 and Spectre #10 to form a panorama.

The Suicide Squad is sent in to destroy the Manhunter's temple in a "Millennium" event crossover. But one of their own turns against them!

The Suicide Squad must transport a bomb into a stronghold of the Manhunters, so stop their attack on Earth. Karin Grace, a member of the original Suicide Squad, reveals that she is actually a member of the Manhunters and betrays her old love, Rick Flag. Realizing that the Manhunter she was in love with is actually an android, Karin Grace decides to transport the bomb herself, dying in the process.

issue_title: Sins of the Father: Part One - Falling Star, Rising Son
description:
With the original Starman retired, his old foe, The Mist, continues an old vendetta against Starman as he returns and takes the life of the hero's oldest son. Now, Starman's rebellious younger son Jack is forced into a role that he does not want and has spent a lifetime denying...

Notes:

  • "Starman" two page text piece with character sketches by Tony Harris.
  • "DC Universe 20" one page Zero Hour advertisement featuring the front page of the Daily Planet with the headline "Zero Hour for Earth?"
  • "DC Universe 21" a one page memorial dedicated to Neal Pozner. Artwork of three headshots of Neal by Phil Jimenez.

issue_title: Sins of the Father: Part Two - Oil (Paint) And Water
description: A riot rocks Opal City while an ailing Ted Knight recovers from a recent attack. The action forces Ted's son Jack Knight to pick up Starman's Cosmic Rod and directly oppose the villainy he swore he'd never face! Is this his calling? Or his doom?

issue_title: The Day Before the Day to Come
description:
Starman learns that another of his father's enemies has returned: Solomon Grundy. Meanwhile, Nash, out for revenge upon the Knight family, takes on the identity of the Mist like her father before her. Plus, Jack has a surprisingly candid chat with The Shade...

After a conversation with The Shade, Jack pays a visit to Charity and runs into Sadie Falk - again.

Later, Jack gets a phone call from Jenny-Lyn Hayden-Scott, Jack goes in search of Solomon Grundy.

Meanwhile, Ted Knight studies Mikaal Tomas.

Elsewhere, Nash furthers her plan of revenge against Jack...

DC's first Starman meets the Starman of the 853rd century in this critical DC One Million tie-in! While Jack Knight continues his epic search through space for Will Payton, Farris Knight, the 853rd century's Starman, pays a visit to Ted Knight at his observatory in Opal City. Ted is shocked and amazed to learn that the name and heroic lineage of Starman resonates so far into the future, but is saddened to learn that the future will find some evil Starmen as well. But which side is Farris Knight truly on?

issue_title: 13 Years Ago: Five Friends - A Tale of Times Past
description:
In this second installment of "Times Past," the Golden Age Flash, Green Lantern, Hourman, Dr. Midnite and Starman band together against Rag Doll and his homicidal cult. Rag Doll plans to overwhelm Opal City in a murderous spree, forcing the five heroes to make a shocking choice.

This issue features Starman/Ted Knight only.

In a second Tale of Times Past, related by The Shade, Starman/ Ted Knight gathers Jay Garrick/The Flash, Alan Scott/The Green Lantern, Rex Tyler/The Hourman and Dr. Charles McNider/Doctor Mid-Nite to confront the wave of chaos perpetrated on Opal City by the Rag Doll cult.

Notes:

  • Ranked #14 in Wizard Magazine's list of "100 Best Single Issue Comics Since You Were Born".

issue_title: Sins of the Child, Part 1: Jack's Day
description:
Nash makes her explosive public debut as the new Mist, and now Jack Knight must run a gauntlet of her fiendish allies to reach his Star Staff. To make sure no one interferes with her plans, the Mist takes steps against Mikaal the alien, Solomon Grundy, and an unsuspecting Ted Knight...

This issue begins Sins of the Child, sequel to Sins of the Father, the arc that introduced Jack Knight created by James Robinson, Tony Harris and team Starman; and, introduced the denizens of Opal City. Nash returns, on a murderous spree this issue, as successor to her father just as Jack is to his father. Jack's Day (The First Half) starts outside the Opal City couthouse, with Ted congratulating his son on being exonerated in Kyle's death. Back at the observatory, they're both surprised when Mikaal and Grundy disappear. While searching for the pair, Jack encounters Nash and her gang.

issue_title: Sins of the Child, Part 2: Ted's Day
description:
Alone and trapped in his observatory, Ted Knight, the Golden Age Starman, must fend off an ambush attack by a newly revitalized Dr. Phosporus. Armed only with his scientific genius and the contents of his laboratory, Knight faces a foe whose very touch means fiery death.

This issue continues Sins of the Child, sequel to Sins of the Father, the arc that introduced Jack Knight created by James Robinson, Tony Harris and team Starman; and, introduced the denizens of . This issue also ties into the Underworld Unleahed mini-series. Nash returns to the Opal, on a murderous spree, as successor to her father just as Jack is to his father. Ted and his son leave the Opal City courthouse, where Jack has been exonerated in Kyle's death. Before heading back to the observatory, the share some time in the park over hot dogs. Back at the observatory, they're both surprised when Mikaal and Grundy disappear. Jack goes off looking for them. When he doesn't come back as he said he would, Ted goes to his friends, The O'Dares at police headquarters. Returning home, Ted encounters and amped up Dr. Phosphorous, hired by Nash to kill him. Dr. Phosphorous, like other rogues, has been amped up by Neron in Underworld Unleashed.

issue_title: Sins of the Child, Part 3: The Opal's Day, The O'Dare's Day
description:
The Mist's carefully orchestrated crime wave washes over Opal City, and a hero from the past is reborn! In a dramatic, kaleidoscopic story focusing on a different character in each segment, Tony Harris shares the pencil chores with Andrew Robinson, Amanda Conner, Chris Sprouse and more.

This issue continues Sins of the Child, sequel to Sins of the Father, the arc that introduced Jack Knight created by James Robinson, Tony Harris and team Starman; and, introduced the denizens of .

Nash returns to the Opal, on a murderous spree, as successor to her father just as Jack is to his father.

issue_title: Sins of the Child, Part 4: Mikaal's Day
description:
Solomon Grundy and Mikaal are kidnapped by the Mist's gang! But when one attacker exhibits a particularly vicious approach to keeping Starman's two friends held captive, Mikaal will need to reach deep down for an explosive escape plan.

This issue continues Sins of the Child, sequel to Sins of the Father, the arc that introduced Jack Knight created by James Robinson, Tony Harris and team Starman; and, introduced the denizens of .

Nash returns to the Opal, on a murderous spree, as successor to her father just as Jack is to his father.

issue_title: Sin's of the Child, Part 5: Jack's Day (The Second Half)
description:
Jack fights his way through an army of assassins to regain his Star Staff for a final confrontation with the Mist. Plus, the fate of Ted Knight, Solomon Grundy, the alien Mikaal, the Shade and the O'Dares is revealed.

Nash has returned to the Opal, on a murderous spree, as successor to her father just as Jack is to his father.

This issue concludes Sins of the Child, sequel to Sins of the Father, the arc that introduced Jack Knight created by James Robinson, Tony Harris and team Starman; and, introduced the denizens of .

In this epilogue to "Sins of the Child," Starman assesses the damage to Opal City and his life. Meanwhile, the Shade continues his search for the poster demon, and the mysterious vision haunting Starman finally surfaces.

It's a tale of "Time Past" as the original Starman confronts his arch-foe, the Mist, during the Golden Age!

Another Tale of Times Past, Ted Knight's first time facing The Mist, as recorded in The Shade's journal.

Jack Knight is once again reunited with his brother David, his immediate--and slain--predecessor as Starman, in this standalone issue. And even though the reunion is bittersweet between the siblings, it's the appearance of another family member that brings Jack to tears.

Talking With David, '96, has Jack and David Knight playing pirate with a surprise waiting for Jack in port.

issue_title: Sins of the Father: Part Three - Mercy
description:
The Mist meets with fellow Starman villain The Shade to form a plan of attack on Opal City while new Starman, Jack Knight, assembles a costume to face The Mist's daughter. But before diving into battle, Jack detours to a fortuneteller store for a quick glimpse at a possible outcome for the battle...

The cover says "December 95" but this is an error as the comic is actually from December 1994.

Part 1 of the 4-part ''Sand and Stars'' storyline! On a quest to uncover the Mist's coveted medal, Starman must leave Opal City and find one of his father's former allies--Wesley Dodds, the Golden Age Sandman!

Following his confrontation with Nash, Jack dreams of her and the two of them together. Oddly his dream ends with an image of the Golden-Age Sandman. After talking to his dad, Jack heads to New York City, and a visit with Wesley Dodds and his paramour, author Dian Belmont.

Starman's search for information behind the Mist turns deadly when he narrowly survives a super-powered assassin's attack and joins forces with the Golden Age Sandman. But Jack may be in over his head.

Adventure finds Jack on his New York visit with Wesley Dodds and Dian Belmont. The Golden-Age Sandman comes out of retirement!

Jack Knight has been captured! As the conflict unfolds and the clock ticks away, the Golden Age Sandman must call on the memory of his first battle alongside the original Starman to save the day in a sequence illustrated by Guy Davis (SANDMAN MYSTERY THEATRE)!

When Jack goes missing, Wesley recalls a previous time he encountered a Starman. The Gambler had kidnapped Ted Knight, The Golden-Age Starman. Dodds stepped in to rescue his colleague, and friend. It may be time for his to step in again.

Time is running out as Starman and the Golden Age Sandman race to find the elusive Nobody before he sabotages an air show, killing hundreds of spectators!

The final act of Jack's adventure in New York with the Golden-Age Sandman, Wesley Dodds and Dian Belmont.

issue_title: Sand and Stars, an Epilogue; Hell and Back, a Prologue
description:
In ''Hellquest'' part 1 of 3, Jack presents the dying Mist with a coveted keepsake and mercifully brings the dying villain a moment of happiness. Later, the O'Dares enlist Starman's aid in rescuing the Shade and Matt O'Dare! Featuring stunning spot art by Chris Sprouse!

After his adventure in New York with Wesley Dodds, The Golden-Age Sandman, and Dian Belmont, Jack visits The Mist to return his lost World War I medal. The Mist sees Jack as his lost son, Kyle. In a brief, touching moment, we get to see a heroic side of this arch-villain.

Leaving The Mist to his own world, Jack is found by Hope O'dare. She has some bad news about her brother Matt and The Shade.

An aside; this issue marks a hiatus for James Robinson on the letter column. He has been alternating excerpts from The Shade's journal and answering letters. Because of deadline issues he is turning over the letter column to Tony Harris with issue 26.

issue_title: To Hell and Back, Part two
description:
Demon Quest: Part Two of Three

Attempting to lure the demonic Merritt out of hiding, Jack Knight uses himself as bait. But even with the help of Opal City's police force, Merritt may prove too formidable a foe even for Starman.

Merrit has gotten word that his poster - the poster he uses to capture souls for a demon - is under guard and will be moved to S.T.A.R. labs in Metropolis two days hence. This is certainly unsettling news.

Jack and the O'dares continue to wait for Merritt to come to them.

He does. Bringing chaos and madness with him.

All hell breaks loose.

Jack goes to Hell.

Demon Quest: Part Three of Three

Trapped in a Wild West version of Hell, Matt O'Dare, the Shade and Jack Knight must defeat the Poster Demon to free the souls of its victims. With the Shade rendered powerless and the Star Staff drained of its cosmic energy, the gamble grows dire as the three realize their very souls are on the line.

Jack arrives to a sight in Hell. Matt O'dare chased by demon cowboys. The Shade dressed all in white.

And the demon.

It's the Christmas season and the O'Dares host a holiday dinner. Many familiar faces appear, but a wayward Santa Claus delays Jack Knight's attendance in this standalone holiday issue.

Christmas at the O'dares. Jack is on his way, cut comes across a down-on-his-luck department store Santa. As the O'dares, Charity, Ted, Mikaal and even The Shade gather; Jack and Santa spread the holiday spirit and clean up the alleys of Opal on their way.

A Tale of Times Past: 1976, Super Freaks and Backstabbers

Set in the disco era, catch a glimpse into the past of the alien Starman, Mikaal. Saving Earth from invasion by his warmongering race, Mikaal lapses into a mire of drugs and apathy. Tomak, the only other survivor of their people, challenges him to a duel to the death in this ''Tale of Times Past.''

In the hazy daze of the Disco era, Starman Mikaal Tomas is confronted by his past. His origins are revealed here.

The Return of Bobo

Opal City is seen through the eyes of a time-lost figure from the past in this special issue that presents a spectacular starting point for new readers! Explore the world of Jack Knight and the entire STARMAN in this perfect introduction to the series!

After a quick recap from The Shade's Journal, we catch up with one Bobo Benetti. While the O'dares keep tabs on him, Jack and Ted learn the latest on Nash. Jack visits Charity. Together, Jack and Bobo face the Royal Flush Gang.

issue_title: Sins of the Father: Part Four - Night F(l)ight
description: To save his father's life, Starman must again face the son of the Mist. Each armed with one of Ted Knight's stellar energy weapons, the two combatants battle in the night sky over Opal City--to the death! Meanwhile, The Shade reveals his own agenda, shifting the balance of power in the city.

Dr. Pip, an eccentric bomber, terrorizes Opal City. Unfortunately, with no demands, even the police can't figure out what motivates the sinister villain. Also, Jack hears from an old ally, for what could be the last time.

As The Infernal Dr. Pip makes his deadly mark on Opal City, one of the residents of the city believes that it is time to make the acquaintance of Jack Knight.

Dr. Pip finds Starman is too much for him to handle, so he brings in some metahuman help--a villain ready to put the bite on Jack Knight. Plus, more on the history of the Black Pirate.

As Jon Valor, The Black Pirate shares the tragic tale of his end with Jack, a mysterious figure hunts transistor radios among the antique shops around the Opal before meeting with The Infernal Mr. Pip!

In part 3 of the 6-part "Infernal Devices," Jack Knight goes up against Copperhead! Now at the mercy of Dr. Pip and his forces, Starman is trapped with the ticking time bomb. A mysterious figure from Jack's past resurfaces, while the Black Pirate races to stop the bomb before it explodes.

The Infernal Dr. Pip continues his mad campaign in the Opal; Jack and Copperhead spar, Mason and the Opal City Police force find Grundy and The Black Pirate introduces himself to Clarence O'Dare!

issue_title: With Some Help from His Friends (Infernal Devices Interlude)
description:
Solomon Grundy lies dying and now Jack Knight, Batman, Sentinel, and the Floronic Man must band together to save the reformed criminal. However, to save the pale giant, they must face past incarnations of Grundy, all of which are evil to the core.

Infernal Devices: Part 4 of 4 seems like such a misnomer. This is more of an interlude, wherein Ted calls in few favors from Alan Scott, Batman and the Floronic Man who join Jack on a fantastic journey inside the comatose Solomon Grundy!

Banding together to save the life of Solomon Grundy, Jack Knight, Batman, Sentinel and the Floronic Man enter the mind of the former villain and find a virtual army of past versions of Grundy. But as the battle rages, Grundy's physical body grows weaker, nearing death.

Jack Knight, Alan Scott, Batman and the Floronic Man take a fantastic journey inside the splintered psyche of Solomon Grundy where they meet Cyrus Gold!

Infernal Devices, part 6 of 6! Respects are paid to the dead, and the cast slowly begins to disperse. But before the final curtain can be drawn, Dr. Pip has one ultimate infernal device--the madman begins his suicide assault on Opal City in an exo-suit laced with explosives!

Returning from the splintered mind of Solomon Grundy, Ted, Jack, Alan Scott and the O'dares are confronted by the infernal Mr. Pip. When the Genesis wave hits, only The Shade has the ability to face Pip.

It's a tale of "Times Past," starring former Starman Will Payton. In a bizarre hunt for a murderous couple working their way across the country, Will reflects on his role as Starman. But things take a bad turn when the chase reaches Turk County and a life is put on the line.

Will Payton, one of many Starmans, is on the trail of a multiple mass murdering couple. He works to save their hostage; this involves playing the killer's question games.

In "Talking with David '97," David brings Jack to a very special dinner party, one featuring the fallen heroes of the All-Star Squadron. The original Black Canary, Hourman, Mr. Terrific, Atom, Dr. Mid-Nite and the Red Bee all share their experiences with Jack--and offer some surprising revelations.

David and a group of dead heroes give advice to Jack over dinner.

issue_title: ... La Fraternite de Justice et Liberte!
description:
In a self-contained story, Ice Maiden, Crimson Fox, Amazing Man II, Blue Devil and Firestorm form the new Justice League Europe! Too bad they're in the way of the Mist's plans. So, the villainess and mother of Jack's child has a simple, but elegant solution to the problem: kill them.

Mist tackles the new Justice League Europe and kills three of its members.

Death of Amazing Man II, Blue Devil, and Crimson Fox.

Notes:

  • Ice Maiden doesn't appear in this issue; it is actually the Mist in disguise.

Part 1 of the four-part "Lightning & Stars" crossover with THE POWER OF SHAZAM! Bulletman, Golden Age hero of World War II, is revealed to have been a Nazi collaborator! As a manhunt ensues, Bulletman flees Fawcett City, seeking aid from one of the few men he can trust: Ted Knight, the original Starman. Ted enlists his son Jack's aid to help hide Bulletman and all seems to be going well... until Captain Marvel finds Jack. Note: "Lightning & Stars" continues in THE POWER OF SHAZAM! #35, also offered this week. ...

With the fall of The Mist, Jack Knight tries putting his life back together. But his attempt to forget Starman proves futile when he receives a disturbing visit from the Golden Age Shade, who reveals strange, hidden facets of Opal City.

Part 3 of the 4-part "Lightning & Stars" crossover! It's the battle of Jack's life when he goes up against Captain Marvel. Possibly the most action-packed issue of Starman ever, this battle promises to be a doozy! Concludes in THE POWER OF SHAZAM! #36.
The Shade and Matt O'Dare cut through Opal City's seedy underworld to protect the secrets of Matt's criminal past. To what lengths are they willing to go to keep his dark secrets?

A "Times Past" story of the Golden Age Starman and the Demon! When a troop of Nazis arrives in 1940s Opal City performing occult rituals, will the Demon Etrigan fight them--or help them? And can Ted Knight come to terms with the Demon's hell-spawned powers?

Jack Knight seeks the help of the JLA as he embarks on an outer-space adventure! Committed to finding former Starman Will Payton, Jack must say good-bye to Opal City and prepare for his perilous journey to the stars. But that journey can't take place without a spacecraft...

issue_title: "1943: Things That Go Bump in the Night"
description:
In this "Times Past" story, the maniacal Prairie Witch returns, but this time, she crosses the bombastic Phantom Lady! Set in the Golden Age, Ted Knight and Phantom Lady join forces to stop her deadly crime spree. But are they strong enough to stop the Prairie Witch's cruel magicks?

Phantom Lady, the cousin of Ted Knight, travels to Opal City in order to find and capture the Praerie Witch, who pulled a robbery at a gala filled with wealthy people back in Washington before starting her crimewave in Opal. Together with Starman, she manages to defeat the Witch and reclaim her lost possessions, as well as the jewelry that has a million dollar reward posted for it, all of which is dedicated to war bonds.
Starman and Mikaal Tomas go into space to search for Will Payton; Bobo Benetti agrees to watch Opal while he's gone. A memoriam of Archie Goodwin.

Bobo Bennetti learns of a plan by the Fiddler, Icicle and Gambler to Kill Starman and saves him with the Shade's help; The Jester teams up with Starman. A good-bye article from regular penciler Tony Harris. James Robinson remembers Archie Goodwin.

issue_title: City Without Light (A Prelude to Bad Times)
description:
Shade and Ted discuss the goings on in Opal since Jack left, including the actions the O'Dares, Bobo and Commissioner Woo; Sadie is approached by the ghost of the Black Pirate who is looking for Jack.

The beginning of the important Two-parter "City Without Light".

issue_title: Starman Blues: Stars My Destination, Part One
description: Jack recounts why he and Mikaal have undertaken this journey; Mikaal has a nightmare and damages the crafts controls; They make an emergency landing on a small blue planet; While exploring, they are attacked by Solomon Grundy.

issue_title: Fighting with Grundy; Talking with David '99
description: While still stranded on the Blue Planet once inhabited by Swamp Thing, Jack Knight is in the fight for his life against Solomon Grundy! Meanwhile, "Talking With David '99" takes on a whole different perspective, as Mikaal discovers some information about the future and the path that he must follow. "Stars My Destination" part 2.

Starman faces Starman when Jack Knight confronts his immediate predecessor--his dead brother, David! David not only wants the mantle of Starman back, but his brother's life, as well. The strange and horrifying battle forces Jack to fight for his own survival...and face his guilt over David's death.

In this issue Jack is reunited with his brother David who is suposed to be dead.

issue_title: Stars My Destination: Lighting the Way: Then, Now and Yet To Be
description:
Special, extra-sized anniversary issue! The two Starmen--Jack and Mikaal--encounter the 30th Century's Legion of Super-Heroes. Teaming up with Legionnaire Star Boy, our heroes finally learn the secrets of Mikaal's cosmic origin, and the fate of Jack's immortal friend, the Shade! "Stars My Destination" part 3.

Jack, Mikaal, and the Mother Box are stranded in 2998 and encounter Star Boy and Umbra from the Legion. They join in the fight against the dark colossus (that transported them to the future in the first place), and find that the cause of it is the Shade, who has survived into the 30th century. Using their cosmic powers, Jack and Mikaal cure the Shade from the "blackness disease" (given to him by his archenemy Culp 1,000 years ago) and thus end the threat of the dark colossus.

Mikaal’s power is restored and he learns from Umbra that he is he is a Talokian like she - and destined to become one of the greatest heroes of their race. Star Boy reluctantly learns from the Shade that he is destined to travel back to the 21st century and become a Starman some time after Jack.

Jack, Mikaal, and the Mother Box leave the 30th century and find themselves transported to the planet Krypton - sixteen years before it exploded.

issue_title: Midnight in the House of El
description: As Jack, Mikaal and a holographic image of the Golden Age Starman continue their search through space for former Starman Will Payton, they arrive on the world of Krypton, decades before its explosion--and meet a teenager named Jor-El! "Stars My Destination" part 4.

Jack Knight, Mikaal and a holographic Ted Knight are journeying through the stars on their search for Will Payton, but that mission may be cut short when Mikaal senses his arch-enemy, the villainous Turran Kha, on a nearby planet--Rann, the adopted world of the hero Adam Strange! "Stars My Destination" part 5.

On the planet Rann, Jack, Adam Strange and Mikaal search for Adam's daughter, Aleea, now held hostage by the murderous villain known as Turran Kha. The odds seem bleak, but our heroes have allies that even they didn't count on! "Stars My Destination" part 6.

issue_title: 1899: The Scalphunter Years: Rich Man's Folly
description: "Stars My Destination" concludes with a step back in time one hundred years long, for a story of old Opal City featuring the Shade and Scalphunter. As an inventor labors at creating "mad science," his family plots his death, hiring an assassin from Gotham City!

Starman Jack Knight and Starman Mikaal Tomas rescue Starfire from space pirates. But how exactly did they accomplish this? One tale told in three different ways as Space Cabbie, Space Ranger and Ultra each narrate their version of the story.

Space Cabbie, Space Ranger and Ultra narrate different versions of a tale concerning Jack Knight and Mikaal Tomas rescuing Starfire from space pirates. The twist being that the identity of said Starfire is different in every version. One features Leonid Konstantinovitch Kovar, the second features Starfire the swordswoman and the third features Koriand'.

issue_title: City without Light, Part II: Bad Times Loom
description: Jack Knight's journey through space nears a surprising conclusion! Tracking former Starman Will Payton's energy signal, Jack and Mikaal arrive at Kranaltine, the Throneworld of the empire ruled by another former Starman. How are the two legacies related? Meanwhile, in Opal City, the O'Dare clan is in the middle of a massive murder investigation in which the prime suespect is none other than The Shade. Complicating the case further is the arrival of several costumed adventurers to the city, among them Phantom Lady, Black Condor, and last, but not least, the Elongated Man!

issue_title: The Stars My Destination: The Welcome Wagon
description: Part 1 of the 4-part conclusion to Jack Knight's incredible journey through space, featuring stunning covers painted by Alex Ross (KINGDOM COME) over pencils by original STARMAN artist Tony Harris! Jack Knight and Mikaal Tomas finally arrive on the planet where Will Payton is being held ? the Throneworld of Prince Gavyn, yet another former Starman. However, freeing Will won't be easy, as Jack and company must do all they can to defeat an array of evil forces in a battle that will forever link all those who have borne the name of Starman. Guest starring the Omega Men's Tigorr and the New Gods' Fastbak!

Part 2 of the 4-part conclusion to Jack Knight's incredible journey through space, featuring stunning covers painted by Alex Ross (KINGDOM COME) over pencils by original STARMAN artist Tony Harris! Jack finally reaches the throneworld once ruled by former Starman Prince Gavyn, where another former Starman, Will Payton, is held captive. Imprisoned by the empire, Jack and Mikaal must launch a revolution to escape, aided by guest-stars Tigorr (of the Omega Men) and Fastbak (of the New Gods). But the biggest shock comes in a surprising revelation on the last page!

issue_title: The Stars My Destination: The Secret of Will Payton
description: Part 3 of the 4-part conclusion to Jack Knight's journey through space, featuring stunning covers painted by Alex Ross (KINGDOM COME) over pencils by original STARMAN artist Tony Harris! The flames of revolution burn brightly on Throneworld as Jack Knight, Mikaal and Will Payton fight to free the empire from tyranny. It's cosmic power versus the might of a hundred planets, featuring Tigorr of the Omega Men and Fastbak of the New Gods!

issue_title: 1882 - Back Stage, Back Then: A Tale of Times Past
description:
Guest artist Teddy Kristiansen illustrates the first in a series of interspersed one-shot stories delving into Opal City's past, drawn from the diaries of the enigmatic Golden Age villain, The Shade. In the 1880s, Shade brings his perverse brand of justice to play against a circus of the damned...

A cold, winter night finds Jack Knight reading The Shade's Journal...

June 1882, Oscar Wilde is on his American tour. He is enjoying an afternoon with The Shade - also known as "Mr. Black" - at the outdoor Cafe de Salle in Opal City. Mr. Black is approached by one Jason Mayville. Mayville seeks to employ Mr. Black to recover his sister from the thrall of the Pepper Stage Troupe and its leader Lune...

issue_title: The Stars My Destination, Finale: Worlds Collide
description: Jack Knight's journey through space concludes in an issue featuring a stunning cover painted by Alex Ross (KINGDOM COME) over pencils by original STARMAN artist Tony Harris! With all appearing to be lost, Jack and his allies must pull miracles from the madness of revolution if they hope to free the empire of the Crown Imperial and finally return home. But even if Jack, Mikaal and Will Payton reach Earth, will Opal be the same city they left behind?

issue_title: In Tranquility and Fire: A Prologue to Grand Guignol
description: Jack Knight's journey through space is over, but it's quiet in Opal...too quiet. It's the quiet before the storm - the biggest storm of evil and darkness Jack will ever face. As Jack begins his investigation into the danger looming over his beloved city, he discovers that many old friends and familiar faces have vanished. This guest-star filled issue sets the stage for an epic war between good and evil that will be waged on Opal's streets - streets that will literally never be the same after this explosive issue.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Premiere Partie: ...And What Went Before
description: Part 1 of the 9-part "Grand Guignol!" The epic war of good and evil begins here, with a look at some crucial events that unfolded in Opal City prior to Jack's return from outer space. Elongated Man, Adam Strange, the Black Pirate, and the Black Condor are among the guest stars investigating the evil that lurks within Opal. At the same time, Phantom Lady has a fateful meeting with the Shade, while Ted Knight recalls a Justice Society adventure that throws an even grimmer light on the Shade and his apparent murders.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Deuxieme Partie: Friends and Foes
description:
Opal City is in flames and all clues point to the Shade. Jack Knight does all he can to stave off the destruction that now lurks around each and every corner of Opal while Black Condor and the Elongated Man do all they can to help. "Grand Guignol" part 2.

Starman tries to deal with his new like with the Justice Society and major disruptions back home, as many of his friends have gone missing.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Troisieme Partie: Fighting with Evil, Talking with David
description: The "Grand Guignol" continues as does the conversation between Mikaal and the ghost of David Knight in "Talking with David ? 2000." Mikaal returns to Opal City and into the arms of his lover, only to have the reunion interrupted by a vision of deceased Starman David Knight, who delves into Mikaal's past. While David learns of the horrors and unspeakable acts Mikaal endured at the hands of the circus freaks, Mikaal confronts the Shade and discovers that all is far from well in the Opal!

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Quatrième Partie: Darkness Not of Night
description: The epic war of good and evil continues as events turn darker still in "Grand Guignol." The Shade seemingly has Opal City in his control with an army of villains doing his bidding. And the only thing standing bewteen them and total victory is Jack Knight. Meanwhile, Ted Knight must fight his own deadly battle with Dr. Phosphorus, a fight where even victory could spell disaster. Who will be the first hero to fall?

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Cinquieme Partie: A Villain's Tale
description:
Last issue, readers learned the dark secret linking the Shade and Culp. Now, a dark, violent tale reveals the full, century-long story of the two shadow-wielders' intertwined, globe-spanning histories! "Grand Guignol" part 5.

The real villain that has conquered Opal City and killed so many is revealed. Culp, a murderous master of the darkness that had been inside Shade for decades.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Sixieme Partie: Rules of Engagement
description: The "Grand Guignol" continues as Opal City's dark war between good and evil escalates. Jack Knight is imprisoned by Culp and his villainous aides, including the Mist, Solomon Grundy and the Rag Doll. With all of Jack's friends and colleagues also held captive, it's up to the three remaining heroes at large to tip the scales: Adam Strange, the Elongated Man and the Black Condor. But are they merely another set of pawns in Culp's ultimate plan? Plus, a tragic revelation about Ted Knight.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Septieme Partie: A Villain's Tale II;  Grand Guignol: Huitieme Partie, A Great Man Recalled... and Recollecting
description:
Loose ends all come together! Culp's mysterious past and his grand, dark plan for Jack Knight and Opal City come to light in an issue featuring appearances by most of the series' roster of characters. "Grand Guignol" part 7.

An army of villains have taken Opal City and a magical barrier prevents any innocents from fleeing. What police left alive are in hiding. The heroes are imprisoned. And the super-villains wonder why they are following and not leading.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Neuvieme Partie: Heroes Reborn, Renewed... and Remembered
description:
As the heroes of Opal City plan their counter-attack against Culp, the new Spider has his first confrontation with the Shade. And at the same time, an introspective Ted Knight recalls the one night when Ted's Golden Age girlfriend, Doris Lee, donned the costume of Starman and had an adventure alongside the original JSA. "Grand Guignol" part 8.

Despairing, ill and lying in a hospital bed while Opal City ticks towards destruction, the original Ted Knight remembers the time someone else wore the Starman colors. And another wore the blue and yellow of Doctor Fate. And on and on, when an entirely new but very familiar Justice League bands together to defeat evil.

Jack Knight visits a sinister circus outside Opal City where he finds a most unsettling freak show--one including a blue-skinned "geek" attraction who may be a former Starman! But Jack's investigation is met with a savage attack from the circus's grotesque performers.

While making his rounds for good deals in Turk County, Jack comes across a circus operated by a Mr. Bliss, and a "Cosmic Geek", Mikaal Tomas.

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Dixieme Partie: The Devil's in the Details
description: As the "Grand Guignol" nears its shattering crescendo, good and evil do battle in the streets of Opal City. See Bobo fight Crusher, Mikaal fight Grundy, Ted Knight fight Phosphorus, Adam Strange face the Bodines, and Jack Knight enmeshed in the struggle of his life against the man called Culp!

issue_title: Grand Guignol, Onzième Partie: Evils Old, New and Unexpected
description: Opal City's dark war between good and evil blazes on as villains are fought, vendettas are sealed, and Jack Knight faces his greatest fear. Heroes from far away and villains from long ago make their unexpected returns as Culp and the Shade finally meet in a battle that will forever decide who shall wield the shadow power. All this, plus a last-page revelation that will shock longtime STARMAN readers!

"Grand Guignol" part 11! All should have been well in Opal--but a new terror has risen that threatens Starman's city. A threat that will destroy the city once and for all unless one hero makes the ultimate sacrifice.

The Mist has hooked himself up to a thrice-redundant dead-man switch hooked up to a nuclear device hidden in the building below him. And then he has taken poison. In five minutes the bomb will flatten what is left of Opal.

Ted Knight swoops down in the biggest cosmic rod he has ever built. He scoops up the building, the bomb and the Mist and takes it all into space. The two reminisce over past encounters and then the bomb goes off, killing them both and harming no one else.

"Grand Guignol" Eulogy. In the aftermath of last issue, Jack and several Golden Age heroes like the Flash, Sentinel and Wildcat gather in a celebration of the life and death of a great hero. Meanwhile, another member of Starman's supporting cast perishes!

Ted Knight's funeral is attended by hundreds. Jack sinks into a deep despair...especially now since his girl has left and his son needs attention he just not sure he can give.

issue_title: A Tale of Times Past, 1899. The Scalphunter Years: His Death and the Dying of It
description:
It's New Year's Eve, 1899, and Brian O'Dare embarks on his last case as the sheriff of Opal City. This is the tragic adventure that cost Scalphunter his life--a dark tale of deception featuring the mysterious Tuesday Club and the bloody war Savage fights with them.

It all starts at the last few days of 1899. Three shopkeepers are being unduly harassed because they will not take a more then generous buy-out offer. Savage, the sheriff, discovers the existence of the Tuesday Club, a group of the city's most prominent men. A calm discussion comes up with nothing. Then the bodies begin to pile up. And heroes will die. And be born.

Guest-starring Superman. Jack Knight has a lot on his mind -- like his thoughts and feelings about Starman, and whether he's still the right man for the job. And who better to discuss heroics with than DC's greatest hero? The "man of the stars" meets the Man of Steel as they discuss fathers, sons, and what it means to be a hero.

Jack and his brother meet for what could be the final time. The secret of how the annual meetings happen is revealed, as David and Jack discuss the history and lineage of Starman.

Jack talks with David one last time and, to gain closure, meets his father. After a happy reuinion and an explanation for these mystical meetings (Kent Nelson) David expects to return home to Opal City. It is Opal...but in 1951!

The much anticipated 3-part storyline, "1951," begins! The penultimate Starman story sends Jack Knight back to Opal's past, to an encounter with the Starman of 1951. This mysterious Starman of yore must unite with Jack in foiling the Mist's plans to steal Opal's scientific secrets, turning the tide of the Cold War in Russia's favor. Who is the Starman of 1951? Action, answers, and the last-minute appearance of a hero from DC's Golden Age!

"1951," Part 2 of 3! Even as the Mist's theft of Opal's science continues, Jack, Hourman and the Starman of 1951 begin to think there's more to the Mist's plans. How do events in 1951 tie into the mental breakdown of Ted Knight? Find out, as Jack Knight's adventure in times past continues.

The conclusion to the 3-part "1951." The Mist's true plans for Opal's stolen science are revealed. Jack, Hourman and the Starman of 1951 know that danger and madness lie ahead if they are to defeat the villain. But is there more to uncover? And with no one left to do so, is the mentally broken Ted Knight up to the job? Old secrets are uncovered and old heroes return to glory in the thrilling penultimate chapter of Starman.

Jack Knight returns to the freak show to free the alien Starman one way or another. But will both Starmen be able to cope with the price of freedom? Plus, a figure from Opal City's past begins to awaken, and a mysterious demon poster returns with its equally mysterious owner.

While bargain-hunting with farmers in Turk County, Jack Knight comes upon a circus, operated by a man named Bliss, and home for a number of freaks including a Cosmic Geek. The other freaks enlist him to champion their escape from Bliss and his assistant Crusher.

Extra-sized final issue. With Jack safely back in Opal City in the present, he must face his greatest challenge yet - turning his back on the city and the Starman lineage for the sake of his young son. But before the end, Jack selects who should take over the cosmic power, and the fate of an O'Dare is revealed.

James Robinson revives his beloved STARMAN series for one more issue as a Black Lantern Starman haunts Opal City. Which Starman has returned and who can stop him from wreaking havoc on the city? Well, the Shade would rather just continue his date with Hope O'Dare, but if no one else can be bothered, what choice does he have but to investigate? Just don't dare call him a Super Hero. As the rest of the DC Universe is learning, defeating Black Lanterns isn't easy - is this the final curtain call for the immortal Shade? Find out in another of this month's one-issue revivals of classic DC Universe titles!

Freeing the alien ex-Starman from the carnival, Jack Knight brings the former captive to his father for safekeeping. Meanwhile, the Mist's daughter breaks out of prison, and the Shade learns that a mysterious killer is causing the citizens of Opal City to disappear, one by one.

After rescuing former Starman Mikaal Tomas from Bliss' freak circus - and freeing the other freaks, too - Jack Knight faces members of the Rag Doll gang.

Nash escapes.

issue_title: A Rage in Arkham, Part One
description:
A Rage is Arkham Part 1 Spinning out of the Bloodline crossover event, Tommy Monaghan is the only hitman in Gotham City to take on super-powered contracts. Using his x-ray vision and telepathy, Tommy has an upper-hand on the criminal element he removes for a cost. However a new million dollar contract puts Tommy within the sights of another Gotham City vigilante. Thus begins one of the greatest comic runs mixing sincerity, violence, paranormal entities, and lots and lots of bullets from some of the most crazed creators in the medium.

Issue one of the acclaimed series from Garth Ennis and John McCrea.

Tommy Monaghan is a hitman specialising in the elimination of superheroes.

A couple of demons from Hell want to recruit him. And they send one of their lieutenants to do the job.

Also, someone wants him to kill...The Joker?! Yes. Joker.

Tommy attempts to escape from the Gotham City Police with a hostage in tow, but just when things seem to go his way, Mr. Truman and Feekle enlist some help to bring him in: Green Lantern Kyle Rayner! "Local Heroes" Part 2!

A police goon squad gather to take Tommy down. Dirty, rotten cops but nothing to kill them over. How can Tommy make it past a dozen well armed officers when he can't even fire a single bullet?

A DC ONE MILLION tie-in! Four teenagers in the far-flung future of the 853rd Century decide to use their father's time-displacement unit to finally fulfill a life-long dream: to meet their favorite legendary super-hero from the past. Tommy Monaghan pays a visit to the 853rd Century!

In the far future iconic items grant common citizens super-powers. The goggles that belong to the explosive hero Gunfire is seen granting the same to another citizen. Naive young men, thinking they can gain power, kidnap Tommy from his bar-seat at Noonan's. Tommy forces them to send him back. Then men then take Etrigan the Demon next; the hell-spawned creature kills them all.
Dark, nasty government forces conspire to hire Tommy. And they've convinced Green Lantern to help them out. How can Tommy sweet-talk a space-cop who can do nearly anything?

The final chapter of "Local Heroes" by Eisner Award-winner Garth Ennis! Tommy confronts Mr. Truman and Feekle, but how will he solve this situation--and what will Green Lantern Kyle Rayner say about his choices?

It's a telepathic Irishman, a naive space-cop and a disgraced Gotham police detective against the worst bastards the CIA has to offer. Pity the government goons.

issue_title: Zombie Night at the Gotham Aquarium Part One of Two
description: Tommy takes an a contract to track down and take out a scientist who can create zombies. Unfortunately the man is one step ahead of them and the Gotham Aquarium is over-taken. And the animals are escaping their cages...

issue_title: Zombie Night at the Gotham Aquarium, Part Two
description:
Zombie humans are one thing, but Tommy Monaghan comes face-to-face with zombie seals, sharks and octopodes! Terrors from the deep arise in "Zombie Night at the Gotham Aquarium" Part 2!

The Gotham Aquarium is now full of bloodthirsty zombie animals. It's time to leave but the place is falling apart...and so is the team.

"Ace of Killers" Part 1! A demonic enemy comes knocking for Tommy Monaghan's soul: Hell's personal hitman, the Mawzir! But how does Catwoman fit into the creature's sudden appearance?

The Mawzir is back to kill Tommy Monaghan, anyone who is with him, nearby police officers...plus he has an army of Mafia mooks to back him up.

After employing the "Cat Signal," things heat up for Tommy Monaghan when Catwoman arrives on the scene. And when it comes to hunting demons, you have to call in an expert: Jason Blood! "Ace of Killers" continues with Part 2.

The Mawzir is after Tommy and his friends. Their only hope is a special gun...which is lost in the depths of Hell!

Tommy, Tiegel, Catwoman and others are trapped in a church under attack by a Mafia goon squad. The Mawzir, who can't actually shoot at consecrated ground, is off slaughtering responding cops. The only hope for anyone inside is Etrigan, deep in the depths of hell, to fetch the Ace of Winchesters, a gun that could kill any demon. But first, Etrigan has to conquer hell itself!

While Etrigan and Baytor battle the Arkannone for the Ace of Winchesters, Tommy, Catwoman, Natt and Tiegel are at the mercy of the Mawzir. But help arrives in the form of...Section Eight? "Ace of Killers," part 4.

Six-Pac tries to rescue his friends by gathering the 'old band', a group of somewhat super-powered lunatics.

Tommy and his friends are making a stand inside a church, with the Mawzir, a demon, eager for their deaths. And the only thing keeping this six-armed gun-demon from joining is that the building is still standing and thus concescrated.

And then the building explodes.

issue_title: A Rage in Arkham, Part Two
description:
A Rage is Arkham Part 2 After last issue's finale, Tommy has to think quickly to escape arrest. Meanwhile the Mawzir begins to track Tommy for recruitment as an agent of the Lords of the Gun. With word out that Tommy has accepted the hit on the Joker, Tommy picks up a list of additional Arkham inmates with hits on their head. Even with Batman watching, Tommy manages to make his way into Arkham, but everything does not turn out as planned.

Tommy has had near-free run of Arkham Asylum, shooting dead many horrible people in order to fill many contracts. But his attempt to do the world a favor by plugging the Joker goes horribly, horribly wrong.

The conclusion to "Ace of Killers!" Out of options and out of ammo, Tommy faces down the Mawzir in a battle for his very soul. But when all seems lost, someone with a few lives to spare might be able to help...

After the high-octane events of the previous arc, Tommy Monaghan finally gets a bit of rest from the super-powered and supernatural--which leaves room for his personal life to go a little crazy when he and Tiegel officially start a relationship!

Tommy's attempt to relax and have a happy day leaves him landing literally in the middle of a deal. He tries to calm the situation but it goes badly and bullets fly and the wrong, wrong people die.The effects of this issue will last through the rest of the series.

It's a holiday-themed HITMAN Christmas special! Everything seems quiet on Christmas Eve, but all heck breaks loose when a radioactive Santa goes on a rampage through the street of Gotham!

Tommy and Natt have no money for Christmas presents this year.

That is until they get a contract to take out a crazed super-villain dressed as Santa Claus.

Notes:

  • Ranked #93 in Wizard Magazine's list of "100 Best Single Issue Comics Since You Were Born".

A new story arc begins with "Who Dares Wins" Part 1. The past comes back to haunt Tommy Monaghan and Natt after a group of S.A.S soldiers are sent to kill the duo as revenge for a "friendly fire" incident during Desert Storm.

A long time ago, a horrible mistake happened in the Iraqi desert. Now the consequences have come home for Tommy and Nat, in the form of British SAS assassins.

British SAS soldiers, some of the best-trained men in all the world, come looking for Tommy and Natt. During the latter's Middle East military service, a horrible accident had occured and they tried to sweep it under the rug. Now it's time to pay the price.

After the blood-filled events of last issue, the S.A.S. go after Tommy through his friends and kidnap Sean Noonan. Can Tommy calm down enough to save his friend...or will yet another buddy's blood leave a stain on his conscience? "Who Dares Wins" Part 3.

A British SAS hit-squad, trying to gain revenge for old friends lost, are having quite a bad-go of it themselves. And the Gotham Mafia is getting angry at things themselves but between Tommy and the best England has to offer, they are just a distraction.

Tommy and Natt fought back against the S.A.S. soldiers, but only succeeded in pushing their enemies even further. They must find a way to even the odds before it not only costs them their lives, but Sean's as well! "Who Dares Wins" Part 4.

Gotham's mafia is picked apart as what was once a 'simple' hit against Tommy and Natt the Hat degenerates into even more death and despair.

In the conclusion to Garth Ennis' latest HITMAN arc, dissention among the ranks of the S.A.S. might give Tommy and Natt the opportunity they need as violence explodes in a vicious final showdown between the duo, the S.A.S. and Men's Room Louie's mob!
The events of the last arc have left Tommy Monaghan experiencing nightmares, night after night. The Hitman has a major crisis of conscience and faith in this aftermath issue to "Who Dare Wins!"

"Tommy's Heroes" Part 1! With the Gotham mobs pinning the massacre at Men Room's Louie's place on Tommy and Natt, the pair join with Ringo and Hacken for a million dollar offer: enlist as mercenaries for six months' work in Central Africa!

issue_title: A Rage in Arkham, Part Three
description:
All hell breaks loose as Hitman realizes too late that his assignment to execute the Joker was a setup: the Mawzir, a gun-wielding demon, is closing in to recruit Tommy Monaghan as an assassin for the Arkanonne, two bullet-ridden demonlords. Meanwhile, Batman is on Hitman's tail as well...and the Dark Knight may be an even bigger problem for Monaghan than going to hell.

Tommy, Batman and a six armed murder-demon are tearing through the basements of Arkham Asylum. Innocent lives are in danger and even the Joker takes a bullet!

Tommy's Central African adventure continues as the crew heads into a village to destroy the rebel food supply. But when Scarlet Rose and Skull begin to murder innocent bystanders, it brings them into direct conflict with Monaghan. "Tommy's Heroes" Part 2.

After turning against the violent acts of their unit, Tommy and Mitchell struggle to make their way across the desert, all while trying to stay ahead of the mercenaries sent to eliminate them! "Tommy's Heroes"Part 3.

Tommy has been scammed by those looking to recruit mercenaries. He thought he was going to assist in saving innocent lives deep in the African desert. But he's stuck with a horrible group of psychopaths fighting...other bastards. It's a real moral dilemma...and then things get much, much worse.

Tommy and the boys meet up with Ributu, the Tynandan rebel leader--but will Tommy use the opportunity to find a way out or will he end up joining the cause? Find out in "Tommy's Heroes" Part 4 of 5.

Good intentions go bad; Tommy and his friends had signed up to help out refugees in a small African country. However, they had been scammed and the goodwill organization is corrupt as the government they are fighting. So Tommy and his friends and a WW2 tank they find...well, somebody's gotta make things right.

The explosive finale of "Tommy's Heroes!" Tommy and his crew bring out the big guns and take the fight directly to Kijaro! But with Scarlet Rose and Skull standing in the way, even the big guns might not be big enough!

Tommy's attempt to do some good has gone completely to hell. He's now stuck deep in the middle of an African country, it's rulers a team of slaughter-happy psychopaths. But what are Tommy and his friends going to have to do to make things right? Are they even any better then those they are fighting?

Of Thee I Sing Superman and Tommy discuss the nature of hope and salvation, after Superman is tested by the expectations of a man he is unable to save. A truly fantastic issue, that outlines the differences of Superman and Tommy through their unique moralistic worldviews and their actions as discrete heroes of the DC universe.

Superman, mistaking Tommy for a casual fan, gets to talking. Superman is suffering a deep depression, he had failed and seen an innocent man die in front of him.

Notes:

  • Ranked #46 in Wizard Magazine's list of "100 Best Single Issue Comics Since You Were Born".

A romantic interlude for Tommy is cut short by the unexpected arrival of Frances Monaghan, the older sister Tommy never knew he had, who brings a dramatic revelation about how Tommy came to be abandoned as an infant!

The dark secrets of Tommy's life finally reveal themselves. Tommy must take a trip for mad killers are on the loose and innocent lives are in danger.

The secret that Sean has kept from Tommy all these years slowly comes to light. Tommy and his newly discovered sister, Frances, trace their mother's horrific final days, days culminating in her death at the hands of Tommy's own father.

Tommy's bastard of a father continues his murderous ways in order to cover past sins. Tommy decides the old man has earned a bullet.

While Tommy hadn't been paying attention, Gotham had gone completely to hell. Various disasters led to the United States government to abandon the city and close it off. This leads to various powers trying to take the city for themselves. Vampires decide to go for 'The Cauldron', Tommy's streets.

With the government having long ago left Gotham City, vampires decide to try to move in, to make it their private feeding ground. Tommy doesn't like this at all so in order to fight them he recruits, well, everyone.

issue_title: For Tomorrow, Part One of Four
description:
Unimaginable secrets of rival assassin Ringo Chen are revealed in "For Tomorrow" part 1! One of the first to come to light is that Ringo just happens to be dating Wendy, Tommy's girlfriend from the first year of the series. And the tension and danger only intensify from there!

Simply because they are so skilled with guns, tensions rise between Tommy and his friend Ringo Chen.

It's never a good idea to get on a mob boss's bad side, particularly when the mob boss is Moe Dubelez, and the bad side is his deceased ""Siamese"" twin, Joe. Joe was offed a while back by Hitman, and has spent the time since busily decomposing and raising a stench only heaven could cure. Seeking vengeance, brother Moe hires his own hitman to kill Tommy Monaghan--a cold-blooded pro named Johnny Navarone.

It's flashback time as someone close to Tommy is destined to die. And his dear friend Natt the Hat has just shown up. So has a bunch of ninja killers.

issue_title: For Tomorrow, Part Two of Four
description:
The tension between Tommy and Ringo escalates, becoming apparent even to the crew at Noonan's. Tommy pays a visit to Wendy to try and defuse the situation--but trouble breaks when Ringo shows up and sees them together! "For Tomorrow" part 2.

Tommy is caught up in a revenge hit on one of his friends, Ringo Chen.

issue_title: For Tomorrow, Part Three of Four
description:
The torture continues for Tommy and Ringo as the Waterman puts the duo through the most horrendous moments of their lives! Plus, even more secrets are revealed about Ringo's past in China and how he made his way to America. "For Tomorrow" part 3.

In between being tortured by Waterman for the benefit of a client, Tommy learns of Ringo's past life, including time spent in the Chinese military.

issue_title: For Tomorrow, Part Four of Four
description:
In "For Tomorrow" part 4, Tommy and Ringo make their final stand against the electric freak known as the Waterman...and at least one participant is not walking away!

Tommy takes down everyone responsible for Ringo's death.

issue_title: The Morning After, The Night Before
description:
After the events of the last arc, Tommy goes to Wendy's and falls into some old habits and makes a decision that he will definitely regret--especially when Teigel finds out about it!

Tommy tries to get his life back together; he and Natt take on the job of killing a pedophile.
